name: Barrel of Barleybrew Scalder
summary: Marleth Barleybrew sends a cask of Scalder toward the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. The ale is meant to prove his brewing against the Thunderbrews, his chief competitors.

sections.title: A Bitter Feud in Dun Morogh
sections.body: The Thunderbrews and Barleybrews compete fiercely over brewing in Dun Morogh. The Thunderbrews are renowned, with their busy distillery in Kharanos. Marleth Barleybrew refuses to live in their shadow. He brews the fiery Scalder to show his recipes can rival theirs, hoping those who taste it will see the Thunderbrews do not own the art of fine dwarven drink.

sections.title: Subterfuge in the Cellar
sections.body: The barrel is meant to be carried into the cellars beneath the Thunderbrew Distillery. There, it will take the place of a cask of Thunder Ale, a local favorite. The plan is a prank born of wounded pride, not poison or ruin: the next batch served upstairs will secretly be Barleybrew's potent Scalder.

faq.q: What is inside the Barrel of Barleybrew Scalder?
faq.answer: The barrel holds Marleth Barleybrew's signature Scalder, a potent dwarven brew made to rival the Thunderbrew family's famed recipes.

faq.q: Why does Marleth want this barrel swapped?
faq.answer: Marleth admits the Thunderbrews make good drinks, but wants them to learn humility. He hopes cellar patrons will taste his brew without knowing it and find Barleybrew craftsmanship just as good, if not better.

aliases: where do i put the barrel
faq.answer: The barrel goes into the cellar beneath the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. It is swapped onto the racks where a cask of Thunder Ale is due to be tapped.

faq.q: Is the brew meant to harm anyone?
faq.answer: No. The brew is a strong, competing dwarven ale. The families' rivalry is intense, but it comes from professional pride, not malice.

angles.text: As a dwarf, you know ale crafting as an art and a bloodsport. Dun Morogh takes its recipe rivalries all the way into the cellar.
As a rogue, you can distract a cellar guard and slip heavy contraband into a guarded stash. It's a low-stakes taste of dwarven subterfuge.
